$comment: What each of the sub-agent's ceilings ships as, and what it may be dragged to. One row per ceiling, and both sides of the seam are emitted from it by `scripts/generate-command-surface.mjs`: `SUBAGENT_BOUNDS` and the `default_subagent_*` functions in `src-tauri/src/settings.rs`, which enforce them, and `DEFAULT_SUBAGENT_SETTINGS` and `SUBAGENT_RANGES` in `src/models/settings.ts`, which offer them. They were twenty-four numbers written twice in two languages with nothing holding them together — a slider that outran the validator would have refused on save, and a default that drifted would have loaded a settings file into a value the validator rejects.
$fieldComment: `field` is the Rust field name, which is `name` in snake_case. It is declared rather than derived so the generator never has to guess how a name breaks into words.
$noteComment: `defaultNote` explains the shipped number and becomes the Rust doc comment. `rangeNote` explains the top of the range and becomes a comment beside the TypeScript row; it is omitted where the range needs no defending. Both are prose, so they are decisions and stay hand-written here.

bounds.name: commandTimeoutMinutes
bounds.summary: Longest one of the sub-agent's tool calls may run, in minutes.
bounds.defaultNote: The bash tool takes an optional timeout and has no default, so a command the model did not bound runs until the machine is rebooted. Five minutes is short because the sub-agent is a reader: it greps, it reads, it summarises output someone else produced. Nothing it is meant to do takes longer, and a command that does is a command it should have bounded itself.

bounds.name: streamInactivityMinutes
bounds.summary: Silence from the model stream, time inside tools excluded, before Gofer asks the endpoint whether it is still there, in minutes.
bounds.defaultNote: Silence is never a verdict on its own. A local model processing a long prompt emits nothing for minutes, and that is work, not a hang. After this long Gofer probes the endpoint: one that answers is left to work and the clock starts over; one that does not is a lost connection. The number only decides how soon a dead server is noticed.

bounds.name: maxTurns
bounds.summary: How many model requests one delegation may make.
bounds.defaultNote: Off. A child that repeats itself is caught by the progress guard, which counts identical calls and results that teach nothing and needs no number sized to a repository. This is a cost cap for a user who wants one; any shipped value is a guess about how large a codebase is, and twenty-four was too few for a large one.

bounds.name: maxAnswerChars
bounds.summary: Longest answer the sub-agent may hand back.
bounds.defaultNote: The whole point is that the raw material stays with the child. Other tool results are bounded at 24,000 characters, so an answer needing more than half of that was never distilled.
bounds.rangeNote: Capped at what a tool result is truncated to anyway (`MAX_TOOL_TEXT_CHARS`): an answer larger than that is cut by the layer above regardless of what is chosen here.

bounds.name: retryAttempts
bounds.summary: How many times a delegation that failed transiently is asked again.
bounds.rangeNote: Attention, not machine time. Past six the conversation has stopped converging and belongs back in the chat, so the top of the range is a ceiling rather than an absence of one.

bounds.name: retryBaseDelaySeconds
bounds.summary: The first wait before a delegation is asked again, in seconds, doubled per attempt.
bounds.defaultNote: Short, because the failure it absorbs is short: one local server with one slot, briefly saturated by the parent and its own child, refusing a connection the next request will get.
